_comment: Single source of truth for system-level (non-npm) binaries this repo shells out to. Read by scripts/check-system-deps.mjs (Gate 1 section + CI install step) — do not hand-maintain a second copy of this list anywhere. Add an entry here BEFORE adding a new execFile/spawnSync/execSync call to an external binary.

binaries.name: magick

debian.install: sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq imagemagick
debian.note: Verified against ubuntu:24.04 (2026-08-27): the `imagemagick` apt package is ImageMagick 6 (apt-cache policy shows only imagemagick-6.q16* candidates) and ships convert/identify/mogrify/composite/etc, WITHOUT the unified `magick` entrypoint IM7 introduced. Installing the apt package alone does NOT satisfy this dependency on Ubuntu. CI additionally installs scripts/ci/magick-shim.sh as /usr/local/bin/magick — a thin dispatcher that forwards `magick <legacy-tool> ...` to the like-named IM6 tool and treats any other first argument as an implicit `convert` call, mirroring IM7's own dispatch rule. macOS's brew formula ships real IM7, so local dev runs the genuine `magick` binary; CI runs the shim. See fallbackShim below.

binaries.warning: Never use `magick` to rasterize SVG in this repo — without the librsvg delegate (which upstream ImageMagick does not ship) it silently drops every stroke (F-040 incident, 2026-08-09; see tools/mapforge/lib/raster.mjs). SVG rasterization is rsvg-convert's job, not magick's, on both the real IM7 binary and the CI shim.

binaries.name: rsvg-convert
binaries.requiredNote: tools/mapforge/tests/*.test.mjs probe with spawnSync("rsvg-convert", ["--version"]) and call t.skip(...) when it's absent — deliberate, not a gap. Installing librsvg2-bin in CI was considered and REJECTED (docs/superpowers/plans/world-fill-STATE.md, 'G-RASTER-BUDGET still runs in ONE venue (Gate 2) and that is a DECISION, not an oversight'): it would put a wall-clock performance assertion on a shared, contended GitHub runner — the exact condition that produced a documented 1-in-8 flaky red on a developer box. The deterministic half of that gate already runs in CI without rsvg-convert. Required for real local map-rendering work (tools/mapforge) and for Gate 2 (scripts/integration.sh), which does have it.

debian.install: sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq librsvg2-bin

binaries.warning: Never substitute ImageMagick for rsvg-convert — see the `magick` entry's warning. tools/mapforge/lib/raster.mjs enforces this at the call site.
